sections.title: Intuition is for everyone, so why is this page created specifically for athletes?

blocks.heading: Because I believe that intuition is essential in sport.
blocks.body: Throughout their careers, most athletes have experienced a powerful connection to their intuition. Moments when they instinctively know what to do, beyond the logical next step, their coach’s instructions or an agreed strategy. They sense an opportunity or anticipate what is about to unfold — and it works, as if something within them recognises the way forward without conscious explanation.

blocks.text: [font=opensans]The momentum, instinct, feel for the game — whatever you call it.[/font]

blocks.body:
[font=opensans][color=blue]It brings an immediate sense of flow and clarity — an inner shift that changes the outer reality.[/color][/font]

[font=opensans][color=blue]The depth of this connection, and how well an athlete can sustain it, can shape their ability to turn difficult situations in their favour, stay present and creative, and enjoy their performance.[/color][/font]

blocks.text:
The only person you are ever competing against is yourself. The rest is out of your control.
— John Wooden, basketball coach.

blocks.body: [font=lora]A space to develop the ability to connect with yourself, listen to your inner voice and recognise what it is saying.[/font]

blocks.heading: [font=lora]Intuition speaks differently to everyone[/font]
blocks.body: [font=opensans]For some, intuition comes as a gut feeling or a sensation in the heart; for others, as a voice, an image, a sudden flash of insight, or even something that appears in a dream. Sometimes it arrives instantly and clearly; at other times it is subtle and needs silence, patience and attention to notice.[/font]

blocks.heading: [font=lora]Where we begin[/font]
blocks.body:
[font=opensans]Our work begins with exploring what intuition means to you: how you naturally perceive it, how it shows up in different situations, and what helps you recognise its signals. You learn to notice, distinguish and interpret these messages, while developing the confidence to trust your own perceptions.[/font]

[font=opensans]As with any new experience, curiosity, courage, openness and trust are essential. Above all, a willingness to explore something new, yet familiar.[/font]

blocks.heading: [font=lora]Inner alignment and trust[/font]
blocks.body:
[font=opensans]Intuition connects us with our inner knowledge, shaped by our experiences, perceptions, feelings and sensations. Yet this journey is not only about understanding and answers. It is also about learning to accept the unknown, the unpredictable and the uncontrollable. Letting go of any boundaries that stand in the way of your inner alignment and contentment is one of the key skills we practice.[/font]

[font=opensans]When we are doing what we love, we don't have to justify it to ourselves or others.[/font]

blocks.text: [font=opensans]Not everything in life can be understood through logic, nor does everything need to be.[/font]

blocks.heading: [font=lora]How the sessions work[/font]
blocks.body:
[font=montserrat]These sessions are led intuitively and individually. There is no predefined programme designed for everyone. My approach is not based on scientific studies or established concepts, but neither does it seek to deny or exclude any particular perspective.[/font]

[font=montserrat]It is not psychological counselling or conventional mental training, though we may touch on some elements of those methods. Sessions normally unfold naturally, instinctively: your intuition will lead us to where your attention and awareness are most needed.[/font]

blocks.alt: Close-up portrait: part of a woman’s face, looking at the camera

blocks.text:
"Faith is rewarded, perhaps, even more than talent or ability. ... We are required to believe in something that doesn't exist in order to allow it to come into being." 
— Rick Rubin, record producer

blocks.title: What we can explore together
blocks.intro: Connecting to intuition on a deeper level can help athletes navigate both sport and life with greater awareness, balance and self-trust. These are a few examples of what we might explore.
blocks.d1: Reducing the emphasis on the result by staying connected to the process rather than fixating on the outcome.
blocks.d2: Tuning in to your inner guidance and learning to distinguish it from fears, mental chatter and external expectations.
blocks.d3: Building a deeper relationship with your body, understanding its sensations and recognising what it is telling you.
blocks.d4: Accepting periods of uncertainty, crisis, rest, growth and change as natural parts of life, and learning to find comfort and joy in them.
blocks.d5: Feeling at ease being yourself and expressing who you are, beyond rigid ideas of what is right or wrong, possible or impossible.
blocks.d6: Exploring and shifting attention and energy towards other meaningful aspects of life, and developing an identity beyond sport.
blocks.finalText: Following your enthusiasm. Seeking what genuinely excites you, with help or despite research, advice or expert opinion.

blocks.text:
"Become who you are."
— Fredrick Nietzsche, philosopher

blocks.heading: [font=lora]Step back from expectations[/font]
blocks.body:
[font=opensans]Sometimes, no matter how much we want to, we struggle to hear or recognise the voice of our intuition.[/font]

[font=opensans]To build a reality of our own, we need to be authentic. We must find strength in who we truly are, rather than sculpting ourselves to fit social standards of success. We must learn to respect our uniqueness — even, and especially, when we mistakenly believe that we are flawed.[/font]

blocks.text: [font=opensans]After years of parental advice, education and social conditioning, in our attempt to fit in, we might drift far away from who we truly are.[/font]

blocks.body: [font=opensans]When this happens, we may begin to recognise it through a persistent internal pressure, overwhelming emotions, an inner void where nothing feels purposeful. Things that once mattered begin to lose their power. What we expected to bring us joy and satisfaction has no such effect.[/font]

blocks.heading: [font=lora]Your inner invitation[/font]
blocks.body:
[font=opensans]Initially, we dismiss these shifts as moods or temporary crises, believing that our next achievement will finally fix everything and make us feel fulfilled and happy.[/font]

[font=opensans]But external changes often bring only momentary relief — a brief moment of ecstasy, soon replaced by the same heaviness and an increasingly desperate pursuit of yet another goal.[/font]

blocks.text: [font=opensans]Perhaps, in the endless marathon of chasing validation, your heavy feelings are a caring invitation to pause, look within and discover what truly makes you feel fulfilled and whole.[/font]

blocks.heading: [font=lora]Unplug[/font]
blocks.body: [font=opensans]When we choose to honour our inner guidance and set out on a path that may be even slightly unconventional, social pressure can become particularly strong. People may offer well-meaning advice and support that simply don't feel right. Setting boundaries to protect our intentions may bring a temporary sense of social alienation — and that's natural.[/font]

blocks.text: [font=opensans]At this point, building a deeper relationship with yourself becomes a priority.[/font]

blocks.body: [font=opensans]You may feel disconnected from everything familiar and still not know what comes next. This space, where you are no longer here but not yet there, deserves to be acknowledged and respected. It is a solid foundation for your new growth.[/font]

blocks.heading: [font=lora]How I can support here[/font]
blocks.body:
[font=montserrat]What I offer is simply a steady presence as you navigate your inner shifts — someone to accompany and support you as you grow more willing to meet your true self and learn to relax into the spontaneity of life, even when it feels uncomfortable.[/font]

[font=montserrat]This is deep and individual work, but having a witness, a friend and perhaps even a guide — someone who can acknowledge your experience, help you make sense of it and remind you that what you are going through is valid and natural — can make the difference.[/font]

blocks.text: [font=serif]My name is Anna Manaeva. Although I am not an athlete myself, sport has always been part of my life.[/font]

blocks.body:
[font=serif]From joining grassroots sports clubs as a child to becoming a passionate sports fan and eventually working as a Competition Manager at one of the world’s largest sports organisations, my journey has taken me through many different sides of sport.[/font]

[font=serif]During my ten years at FIFA, I contributed to the organisation of football World Cups, as well as numerous related events. Along the way, I met athletes at different stages of their careers, each with their own backgrounds, experiences, ambitions, and challenges. Through these encounters, I gradually developed a deeper interest in the person behind the athlete — their individual journey, their inner world, and the challenges that may remain unseen from the outside. Over time, I began to envision a space where athletes could find support beyond their sporting achievements.[/font]

[font=serif]A few years ago, my own life took a turn that had been brewing within me for some time. I left what many would call a successful career without knowing what would come next. This gave me — or, honestly, pushed me into — the space to pause and look inward, to reflect on who I really am and what I truly want.
I delved into psychology, body and energy practices, alternative medicine and healing approaches, as well as ancient philosophies. I explored my own perceptions and senses, experimented and gradually discovered new ways of understanding myself and the world around me.
Most importantly, I started to embrace life as an exciting adventure to be experienced now, rather than a constant pursuit of security for tomorrow.[/font]

[font=serif]I have always been intuitive. Unfortunately, my sensitivity wasn't appreciated and was often dismissed by family and teachers during my early years, so I never really learned to trust it.
Over the past few years, however, I have managed to find my own voice beneath layers of outside noise. I have begun to trust myself more deeply, rely less on external validation and let go of the need for constant prediction and control.[/font]

blocks.text: [font=serif]Today, through the sessions I offer, I am bringing this idea of creating a supportive space for athletes to life. Guiding others in their search for self-trust, fulfilment, and happiness has become a meaningful part of my own journey.[/font]
